evals.prompt: My Obsidian vault has a lot of notes and I suspect some are unreachable. Build a graph from /path/to/vault and tell me which notes have no meaningful links, then show me how you would fix three of them.
evals.expected_output: A check+build sequence with the graph kept outside the vault, an orphan query using file_path IS NOT NULL, a list of orphan note ids, and three link proposals each carrying its evidence query and row.

evals.prompt: Why does every link in my vault come out as LINKS_TO even though I wrote them under headings like 'Related topics' and 'Dependencies'?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of the edge-type ladder (brace, link title, heading_edges, built-in substring ladder), why structure/heading_edges declarations are needed, and the concrete fix plus the query to verify the retyping.

evals.prompt: Turn this vault into something another agent can query over MCP, and give it three canned questions it can call directly.
evals.expected_output: A --vault or --graph server command, a .kglite/recipes/ file per canned question with a valid parameters schema, the LIMIT 200 rule respected, and the restart-vs-rebuild lifecycle explained.

evals.prompt: I want the link graph visible inside Obsidian itself, and I also want to be able to push changes from the graph back into the vault without breaking my notes. How do I prove the round trip is lossless?
evals.expected_output: A choice between canvas (never parsed), a kg_skip backlinks index (idempotent, no feedback), and a sealed export; the sealed pipeline copies .kglite/vault.yaml and removes frontmatter keys the body already states; vault_roundtrip.py is run and its seven checks plus the documented edge-property loss are explained.
